There is no manual QC or editing beyond visual checks.
The metadata warns about possible misclassification of unmapped objects.

The SurfZone DEM was produced in 2019.

OS Terrain 5 is a detailed digital terrain model of Great Britain.
It is available as a grid of heighted points and as contours.
Publication months are January, April, July and October.
Documented uses include asset and site management.
The documentation lists product scale as 1:10,000.
OS Terrain 5 is the mid-resolution OS terrain product.
It is designed to interoperate with large-scale OS data.
Grid and contour products are supplied as 5 by 5 kilometre tiles.
The grid uses regular 5 metre post spacing.
Standard contour polylines use 5 metre vertical intervals.
Index contours occur at 25 metre intervals.
Contours include mean high and mean low water boundaries.
The product has full Great Britain coverage.
Grid data is available in ASCII grid and GML 3.2.1.
Contours are available in GML 3.2.1 and Esri shapefile.
Grid and contours are created from the same source data.
Tiles are identified by the National Grid reference of their south-west corner.
GML features and geometries require unique identifiers.
Terrain 5 feature identifiers follow an os.t5 tile-and-sequence pattern.
Geometry identifiers use the feature pattern with a .geom suffix.
Updates are supplied by whole-tile refresh.
Sequential identifiers are regenerated when a tile is updated.
GML geometries use EPSG:27700 expressed as an OGC URN.
The grid GML supplies metadata rather than the external height block.
Spatial height values are carried in the ASCII grid external block.
Each grid value is the mean height across its 5 metre pixel.
The first value is positioned 2.5 metres from the tile's north-west corner.
Grid heights are given to the nearest 0.01 metre.
The download includes a PRJ spatial-reference file.
The download includes an asc.aux.xml styling file.
It uses the GML simple-features level-0 profile.
XML schemas validate GML format and content.
Spot heights are selected by an automated process.
The process selects the highest mass point inside a closed contour.
The selected point must differ from the enclosing contour by at least 1 metre.
Spot-height z values are rounded to one decimal place.
A full compressed national grid supply is approximately 16 GB.
